Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on February 1, 2025
Review Body:
You should really only purchase this if it's your intention to donate to the Trump family. I'm sorry, but all of the five-star reviews are merely political-based. I read this book before the election, and I reserved my rating (on Goodreads and on here, obviously) until after, so that I wouldn't be accused of bias. I really wanted to get to know Melania. She is often - I believe, unfairly - given far too much criticism in the press, when she is merely keeping to herself (as is her right). What I don't appreciate in books, however, and what ultimately causes me to give them the lowest ratings, is when they're advertised as something other than they actually are.

In this case, this is NOT a memoir. You are not going to learn anything about Melania that are don't already know, or that a quick Wikipedia search won't tell you. Except maybe how committed she was to remodeling different rooms that were falling into disrepair in the White House? She goes on at length about how she personally embroidered a rug in one room, chose the curtains for another, etc... not that that's not cool, but I really didn't care to read 30 pages of a 182 page book about it (never mind that 30% of the book is pictures). I've always thought there was a lot more to her than meets the eye, that she obviously got into a great architecture school back home in Slovenia for a reason - and I was really hoping that this would be more than just an attempt to swing voters onto the Trump ticket. It wasn't. Maybe that will come at another point, but I'm not holding out much hope. There are a few interesting facts, like about how her leaked nude modeling photos were taken when she was like 21 years old and she successfully sued the photographer (none of which we hear about, of course). Also, how the jacket she wore stating something along the lines of "DON'T CARE DO U?" was more of a middle finger to the paparazzi, who instead attributed it to her feelings about the children being detained at the border. I wish we'd gotten to hear more of this kind of thing. I didn't expect it to be a sizzling tell-all at such a politically tense time, but I did expect a little more than what I got. Unless what you're looking for is glossy photos and glowing reviews of how great Donald is as a father and husband behind closed doors, wait for the paperback... or better yet, wait for an actual memoir.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 22, 2025
Review Body: Hmm... what did I think about Melania Trump's memoir MELANIA? That requires some pondering. While I did learn about her childhood, family, education, early-and-later career movements in the first few chapters, and unequivocable commitment to her son, the majority of the book read like an endless detailed list of tasks and events perfectly monitored by an extremely disciplined woman and later dedicated First Lady. (I didn't say she was, I said that's what her own appraisal of her time there sounded like.) She is one confident, self-assured woman, for sure, and she tells us so---many, many times. I can't recall ever reading one time where she stated a weakness or failing of her own. However, there's no doubt as to her extreme dislike of the media, but that is probably totally justified. As with any other human, there are qualities she seems to have that I admire and appreciate, but in the latter pages, I definitely learned of serious values she holds that are totally opposite of mine, and they are, in my opinion, crucial values. I do applaud Melania for having the nerve to state them regardless of what anyone thinks. We all know, however, knowing someone personally is the only way to truly know someone. Reading what they choose to tell you about themselves in typed word is very subjective and hardly a fair representation of the real person. And let's face it, a plain, everyday woman like me cannot relate at all to Melania's upper-class lifestyle. Could I walk even a half-mile in her shoes? No, I don't think so, nor do I want to (even if they were flats). But I'm more interested in the inner person she is than actions she executes. The writing itself was not very good with far too much repetitive thought, a gazillion "I"s, and endless listing of perceived accomplishments. Frankly, I was disappointed in the book and have a reduced appreciation for the lady because of the massive self-promotion and certain critical opposing values. Read it for yourself, and see what you think.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on December 4, 2024
Review Body:
I was lucky. No damage to the book. The cover had issues but survived a complete reading looking good. Photos, and there are many, did not fall out but some were too small to see well or out of focus. The price was right for a hard cover book. Thank you, Amazon! I did not expect the first lady who is approaching a race for a second term in the White House to enter any discussion of her husband's affairs. The book seems to have been a promotional effort in a tight race to see the first family in a favorable light, so I did my best to read it with that in mind. I am not a Trump supporter. The book is easy to read. Vocabulary is limited and allows for quickly moving through the pages. The book does share early years in Europe, life with her parents and sister, the development of her modeling career. It was enjoyable. Her courtship and marriage was handled gracefully. She makes it clear that she adores her son, Barron, and I did enjoy seeing photos of him with his father as a baby and young boy. She makes an effort to "correct" information that was harmful to the family. I understand....

What was missing, even though an effort was made, was tender warmth toward "Donald" or his existing family. She does say that she didn't always agree with him. She made it clear that she was disappointed that children were separated from families at the border. She doesn't nearly cover the Covid 19 epidemic as well as I would have liked, but she shares the White House suffered with the president, herself, Barron all infected. But not much about other Americans. She doesn't describe the Jan 6, 2020 riot and the threat it brought to lives and the cost to America's property and process. It is barely mentioned. The omission glares. Trump's refusal to accept defeat for the election was not mentioned at all.

I am happy to have read the book. It gave me insights about her and some formal policy too. There is no mention or acknowledgements of anyone for the writing. Surely, she didn't produce this solo. I also came to appreciate that First Ladies have more responsibilities than I imagined and staff too. There is a fragile balance between privacy and sharing important truths. The reader will have to decide.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on October 12, 2024
Review Body: Melania is a fascinating person on many levels, not the least is her account of what goes into her understated and elegant appearance. She admits she finds great joy in grooming and dressing herself to look perfect at all times, even when her calendar permits a day off. If just half of what she claims about herself and her accomplishments are true, then she's quite exceptional. She is not shy about boasting about her achievements AND her natural beauty. Not everything rings true on these pages, except for her love of her family, her son and yes, her husband. She does reveal enough about herself, in particular, her need for order, privacy and beauty. There isn't a lot of meat with the potatoes, as it's clearly been written and published to win favor supporting her husband's candidacy portraying herself as the textbook perfect First Lady. Since English is not her first language, one can excuse the poor grammar, but what's inexcusable is the editing, or lack thereof. Even photo captions indicate lack of attention to detail. Examples: "Donald and I with Barron." "My mother and I at the White House." Her insistence on need for perfection doesn't ring true when the entire book is filled with grammatical and historical inaccuracies. The proof-readers and editor(s) failed to do their jobs professionally. This is a publication that was obviously rushed to be released before November 11. Unlike other reviewers here, I found the book styling to be in concert with her understated, elegant pubic image. Fortunately my copy arrived clean, pristine and intact.
